reason: `java.util.Date`’s equals method returns true when compared with a `java.sql.Timestamp` that has the same millisecond value, but `java.sql.Timestamp`’s equals method requires the other object to be a `Timestamp` as well. Thus `method1` evaluates `apple.equals(orange)` as true but `orange.equals(apple)` as false, yielding false, whereas `method2` only checks `a.equals(b)` and returns true.
